subject: Operational dependency mapping for Private/VPC & on-prem feasibility review
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational dependency mapping for Private/VPC & on-prem feasibility review

Team —

As discussed in last week's product sync, Northbridge Health has asked us to validate feasibility for a mixed Private/VPC + on-prem deployment pattern. I attached an initial dependency matrix (vpc-deps-matrix.csv) with the items I could pull from the discovery notes.

Top asks from product:
- Confirm the end-to-end integration dependencies (networking, peering, KMS, audit log shipping).
- Provide a conservative resourcing estimate (SRE/infra FTEs and on-call) for a pilot vs GA.
- Call out any blockers that would require an exception to our standard Private offering (air-gapped, custom NACLs, non-standard KMS).

Please review the matrix and add rows where we don't yet have vendor or infra inputs. Marcus — can you fill the runtime/kv-cache and model-quantization dependencies? Kimberly — flag any compliance gating items. Grace — prioritize which product features we must guarantee for the pilot so we can scope effort.

I want a one-page decision brief by EOD Thu 9/16 that we can present to Legal and Sales. If that's not feasible, reply with the minimum deliverable and blockers.

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference

Attachment: vpc-deps-matrix.csv (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational dependency mapping for Private/VPC & on-prem feasibility review

Jonas / team —

I pulled the runtime and infra dependency sections and added a first pass to vpc-deps-matrix.csv. Key technical points:

- KV cache warmup requires persistent storage that we currently assume in the VPC. On-prem nodes will need a replicated SSD-backed cache or a fast NFS mount; this adds ~0.5-1.0 FTE infra ops to manage replication and recovery during pilot.
- Quantization variants: our 4-bit path is supported on the Dedicated runtime but needs QA on the on-prem runtime; plan 2 weeks QA for the critical model family.
- Networking: L3 peering + static routes preferred. If Northbridge insists on private circuits (MPLS), schedule adds 4-6 weeks and vendor coordination (ThirdWave).

Open questions added in the sheet (column: OWNER): ThirdWave connectivity, KMS integration pattern, and backup retention differential for on-prem.

I can take the lead on the runtime verification and prepare the infra staff-hour estimate if we agree on pilot scope.

—Marcus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational dependency mapping for Private/VPC & on-prem feasibility review

Thanks Marcus — that clarifies a lot. From product perspective the pilot must support:

1) Single-tenant model pinning (we can't rely on shared catalog updates during pilot)
2) Low-latency SLOs for 95th percentile inference across the hybrid path (we'll provide sample traffic)
3) Audit log retention and searchability for 90 days (Security will verify)

If the on-prem KV approach adds 0.5-1.0 FTE to manage replication, we should compare cost vs a blended route where cache remains in our VPC and only compute is on-prem. If ThirdWave connectivity takes 4-6 weeks that pushes pilot start to late Oct, which is outside Sales' internal target.

Deliverable ask: please produce a concise option matrix with cost/latency/resourcing tradeoffs (pilot vs blended vs full on-prem) by Thu EOD so Sales can set customer expectations.

Grace
Group Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the matrix. Northbridge can confirm they have a colo cage in our preferred datacenter and can provision a private circuit with ThirdWave. We prefer a full on-prem compute foot in the pilot but are open to a blended approach if it shortens time-to-demo.

Notes from infra: we need a minimal hardware spec from you (CPU/GPU count, NICs, rack space) and a terraform snippet for our networking team to evaluate (we attached northbridge-iac-snippet.tf). ThirdWave is cc'd to confirm circuit timings.

Pamela Lowe
VP Infrastructure, Northbridge Health

Attachment: northbridge-iac-snippet.tf (text, 84 lines)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational dependency mapping for Private/VPC & on-prem feasibility review

Quick compliance checkpoint —

- KMS: on-prem integration will need an HSM-backed KMS or MFA-proxied calls to customer KMS. If Northbridge will host their own HSM, we need an exceptions form and an HSM integration test plan.
- Audit logs: ensure log-forwarding to a secured S3 bucket or our log-collector appliance; retention differences will require policy sign-off.
- Data residency: confirm that any model weights we store on-prem do not get copied back to shared buckets. We will document an isolation pattern in the brief.

I'm attaching a short hardware security checklist that we recommend for on-prem pilots. This will also impact ops FTE estimates.

Attachment: onprem-hw-reqs.pdf (pdf, 7 pages)

Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>

Thanks everyone — good progress. Short summary and action items (for the Thursday brief):

- Marcus: finish the option matrix (pilot vs blended vs full on-prem) with estimated infra FTEs and a two-week QA plan for quantization variants. Due: Tue 9/21.
- Kimberly: draft the exceptions form and the HSM integration test plan; include the hardware checklist. Due: Wed 9/22.
- Grace: prioritize pilot feature set (1–3) and confirm the traffic shape for latency checks. Due: Wed 9/22.
- Pamela / Northbridge: confirm circuit lead time and share rack/cage appointment window. Northbridge to confirm by Mon 9/20.

I built a short decision brief template in the Drive link (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleDriveLink) and will slot the artifacts as they arrive. If we hit the 4–6 week circuit cadence, we present a blended-route as the default to keep the demo in Oct.

I'll book a 30-minute alignment call for Tue 9/21 10:00am PT unless someone replies with a conflict.
